what_worked: Whitespace scatter and prioritization matrix synthesize multiple dimensions into genuinely actionable strategic recommendations.
fix_next: Reconcile total revenue ($13.47M vs actual $15.60M) and verify every category median against the source data before presenting.
verdict: Strong strategic arc undermined by materially wrong revenue totals and category medians.
factual_error_detail: Slide 3/4: Total MRR $13.47M vs actual $15.60M (~$2.1M understatement). Slide 3/6: Top-10 share 48% vs actual 49.6%. Slide 8/10: Education median $2,142 vs actual $2,435; Marketing median $1,586 vs actual $2,369.50; Analytics median $1,294 vs actual $419 (massively overstated—direction-reversing error); AI median $446 vs actual $503; Dev Tools median $185 vs actual $635. The Analytics error is especially damaging: it is presented as a high-monetization category justifying investment, when its true median is among the lowest.

evidence.insight: Slide 11 count-vs-median scatter and slide 13 monetization-vs-effort 2x2 are original synthesizing views; the AI-is-crowded-and-underpaying thesis is decision-useful. However, the Analytics misplacement weakens the framework's credibility.
evidence.narrative: Clear purposeful arc: scale→growth→concentration→segments→monetization→effort→synthesis→risks→prioritization→recommendations. Now/Next/Later on slide 14 lands well. Coherent thesis throughout.
evidence.framing: Slide 2 sets scope, audience, and data caveats explicitly. Slide 12 dedicates a full page to six specific risks including missingness (29% audience gap), self-reporting, and proxy limitations. 'Senior management' audience is stated.
evidence.accuracy: Total revenue understated by ~$2.1M. Multiple category medians are materially wrong. Analytics median is overstated by ~3x ($1,294 shown vs $419 actual), which reverses its strategic positioning—it is presented as a high-monetization whitespace opportunity when it is actually mid-to-low. Marketing overstated by ~$784. Education off by ~$293. Dev Tools understated by ~$450. These errors propagate into slides 10, 11, 13, and 14, corrupting the core strategic recommendations.
evidence.visual: Consistent navy/gold palette with clear hierarchy, well-annotated bar charts, effective callout boxes. Scatter plots on slides 11 and 13 are well-designed with quadrant labels and color coding. Donut chart on slide 5 is appropriate. No chartjunk or decorative filler. Slide density is well-managed throughout.
evidence.ai_slop: Mild consulting-speak on title slide ('Strategic Intelligence Briefing') but content is substantive and dataset-specific throughout. No generic filler or decorative-but-meaningless graphics.

change_reason: Lowered accuracy from 5.5 to 5.0: the Analytics median error ($1,294 shown vs $419 actual) is direction-reversing and propagates into the core strategic recommendations on slides 10, 11, 13, and 14. Reduced bonus from 2 to 1: the prioritization framework is genuinely creative but its credibility is undermined by the erroneous inputs feeding it.
